decisions.element: Front door — glass above the door
decisions.title: Front door — glass above the door
decisions.context: The plain radiating-muntin fanlight is out. Both remaining options use warped, hand-blown glass — the question is how it's held. A quieter Option B (tracery only, no bullseyes) exists on request.

options.label: A — The 72
options.caption: Flat four-light transom · crown-glass bullseyes · straight entablature
options.ancestorTrace: Glebe bones reshaped · Captain Jack's glazing

options.label: C — The Lens
options.caption: Semi-circular fanlight · fine tracery · crown-glass bullion at the hub
options.ancestorTrace: Glebe bones intact · Captain Jack's glazing at the hub

decisions.element: Wharf Wing — the Glass Bridge seam
decisions.title: Wharf Wing — the Glass Bridge seam
decisions.context: The Wharf Wing is moving to a two-siding scheme: white-painted clapboard on the gables, weathered grey cedar shingle on the flanks. Where the wing meets the Glass Bridge, the shingle can return around the bridge-side gable — keeping the named limestone↔shingle seam — or the gable can go clapboard, so the seam becomes limestone↔clapboard.

options.label: Shingle returns around the bridge-side gable
options.caption: Grey shingle turns the corner and meets the glass walkway.

options.label: Gable goes clapboard
options.caption: White siding meets the glass walkway; grey stays on the long side.

decisions.title: Wharf Wing — shutter color
decisions.context: The compound-wide lock is dark green shutters. But the Wharf Wing trim rule is blue-family only — no greens — and the Captain Jack's reference building wears blue shutters.

options.label: Blue-family
options.caption: Matches the Wharf Wing trim rule and the Captain Jack's reference.
